papers.title: Magneto-optical study of Nb thin films for superconducting qubits
papers.abstract: Among the recognized sources of decoherence in superconducting qubits, the spatial inhomogeneity of the superconducting state and the possible presence of magnetic-flux vortices remain comparatively underexplored. Niobium is commonly used as a structural material in transmon qubits that host Josephson junctions, and excess dissipation anywhere in the transmon can become a bottleneck that limits overall quantum performance. The metal/substrate interfacial layer may simultaneously host pair-breaking loss channels (e.g., two-level systems, TLS) and control thermal transport, thereby affecting dissipation and temperature stability. Here, we use quantitative magneto-optical imaging of the magnetic-flux distribution to characterize the homogeneity of the superconducting state and the critical current density, $j_{c}$, in niobium films fabricated under different sputtering conditions. The imaging reveals distinct flux-penetration regimes, ranging from a nearly ideal Bean critical state to strongly nonuniform thermo-magnetic dendritic avalanches. By fitting the measured magnetic-induction profiles, we extract $j_{c}$ and correlate it with film physical properties and with measured qubit internal quality factors. Our results indicate that the Nb/Si interlayer can be a significant contributor to decoherence and should be considered an important factor that must be optimized.

summary.summary: Magneto-optical imaging of Nb thin films reveals distinct flux-penetration regimes—from Bean critical states to thermo-magnetic dendritic avalanches—that correlate with film microstructure and quality factors in superconducting qubits. The Nb/Si interfacial layer emerges as a critical decoherence bottleneck, with optimal thermal coupling and superconducting order parameter achieved through high-power DC sputtering (sample C), which balances flux screening with thermal stability.
summary.motivation: Superconducting Nb thin-film qubits achieve lower coherence than bulk Nb cavities ($Q_i > 2$ s photon lifetime), and the spatial inhomogeneity of the superconducting state and interfacial properties remain underexplored as decoherence sources despite their potential impact on transmon performance.
summary.method: Three Nb films (175 nm on Si) were deposited via HiPIMS and DC sputtering at different rates and characterized by Faraday-rotation magneto-optical imaging at 4 K and 6 K with perpendicular applied fields of 40–320 Oe, with magnetic induction profiles fitted to the Bean model to extract critical current density $j_c$ and correlated with grain size, resistivity ratio ($\mathrm{RRR}$), and measured internal quality factors.
summary.result: Sample C (DC sputtering, 25 nm/min) showed the highest $Q_i$ with excellent flux screening comparable to sample B but superior thermal coupling via the thinnest uniform silicide interlayer, while sample B exhibited strong pinning ($j_c$) but pronounced dendritic avalanches at both 4 K and 6 K, indicating poor thermal conductance to the substrate.
